description: Advisory mutation-diff lane waivers (an earlier decision / L2, an earlier decision). Each waiver suppresses ONE survivor (one concrete operator, on one line-content, in one definition) from the advisory report's un-waived total. Identity is content-based, NOT line numbers: the fingerprint folds module + enclosing definition + operator + the normalized mutated line, so a waiver survives a function moving but dies when its line's content changes. Rules (checked by scripts/mutation_waivers.py): required fields, single concrete operator + file + definition (no wildcard/file-wide/operator-wide waivers), classification from the fixed vocabulary, mandatory reason + evidence, dated re-verification, pinned tool version. Approval is human-only: a waiver suppresses only when approved_by == 'human'; the AI submits with approved_by=null (pending) and never self-approves. Nothing here gates CI yet — enforcement is L6 (#299). See scripts/mutation_waivers.py for the authority.

waivers.reason: The '|' being mutated is inside the type annotation `agent_id: str | None`. cpersona/isolation.py opens with `from __future__ import annotations`, so under PEP 563 every annotation is stored as an un-evaluated string and never executed. The BitOr->Add mutant (`str + None`) therefore has no runtime effect and no test can observe it — this is engine noise, not a missing test. The same annotation-`|` noise recurs on the sibling axes (project_id / channel) and across the codebase; it is the first candidate for an operators-filter exclusion once L6 (#299) weighs the noise rate.
waivers.evidence: structural: `from __future__ import annotations` at the top of cpersona/isolation.py; PEP 563 makes all annotations non-evaluated strings
